caution.note: Tailwind's orange-400. The only significant color in the system that is not a project token.

restricted.note: Marks privilege, not state. Always arrives as a dashed border, never a fill.

paper.note: Page ground. Carries hue 165 even at 99.5% lightness.

surface.note: Panel fill. The tonal step from Paper is the elevation; there is no shadow.

ink.note: The one neutral that shifts cool-blue rather than green in light mode.

hairline.note: Becomes translucent white in dark mode so it reads over any surface.

display.purpose: Page titles only. One per page. Lora at 700.

title.purpose: Panel and dialog titles on a bottom-ruled header. Lora at 500, small.

body.purpose: System default inside every component. 12px, line-height 1.625.

label.purpose: The HORUS · [SECTION] breadcrumb and small-caps metadata. Uppercase, 0.1em tracking.

numeral.purpose: Standalone figures — queue counts, ticket age, chart totals. Always paired with a muted caption.

mono.purpose: Chart tooltip values with tabular-nums. Loaded and available but almost entirely unclaimed.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: This system has no box-shadows. Depth is a hairline ring plus a tonal step. Adding one would dominate the interface.

shadows.name: panel-ring
shadows.purpose: The universal container edge. Drawn in foreground color at low alpha so it adapts across both themes from one declaration.

shadows.name: modal-scrim
shadows.purpose: The only true layering event in the system. Carried by the backdrop, never by a shadow on the dialog.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Button :active nudge. Suppressed on menu triggers so popovers don't jump.

motion.name: hover-nudge
motion.purpose: The directory card's chevron slides 4px right on hover. The system's only decorative motion.

motion.name: overlay
motion.purpose: Dialog and popover enter/exit. Deliberately fast.

motion.name: icon-gesture
motion.purpose: Sun, moon and cog icons animate on interaction. The entire non-CSS motion vocabulary.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one solid-filled surface in the system. Use for the single real action on a screen.

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action. Hairline border on the page ground, filling muted on hover.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-outline">Open random<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M7 7h10v10"/><path d="M7 17 17 7"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.375rem; height: 2rem; padding: 0 0.625rem; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 0; background: var(--background); color: var(--foreground); font-family: var(--font-sans), sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.15s ease; outline: none; } .ds-btn-outline svg { width: 1rem; height: 1rem; pointer-events: none; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--muted); color: var(--foreground); } .ds-btn-outline:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Panel
components.description: The universal container: square, ringed, never shadowed, with a Lora-set ruled header.
components.html:
Unassigned queue
Nothing lifts, nothing rounds. The ring is the edge and the tonal step is the elevation.
components.css: .ds-card { --card-spacing: 1rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--card-spacing); padding-block: var(--card-spacing); border-radius: 0; overflow: hidden; background: var(--card); color: var(--card-foreground); font-family: var(--font-sans), sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; line-height: 1.625; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklch, var(--foreground) 10%, transparent); } .ds-card-header { display: grid; gap: 0.25rem; padding-inline: var(--card-spacing); padding-bottom: var(--card-spacing); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); } .ds-card-title { font-family: var(--font-heading), Georgia, serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; } .ds-card-content { padding-inline: var(--card-spacing); color: var(--muted-foreground); }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: The Three-State Rule made visible. A 10% tint of the state hue behind text of the same hue, never a solid fill.
components.html: Waiting In Progress Closed
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.25rem; height: 1.25rem; padding: 0.125rem 0.5rem; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 0; font-family: var(--font-sans), sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-badge-waiting { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--destructive) 10%, transparent); color: var(--destructive); } .ds-badge-progress { background: color-mix(in oklch, oklch(0.75 0.183 55.934) 10%, transparent); color: oklch(0.75 0.183 55.934); } .ds-badge-resolved { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary) 10%, transparent); color: var(--primary); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Transparent fill, hairline border, square. Focus matches the button treatment exactly.
components.css: .ds-input { height: 2rem; width: 100%; min-width: 0; padding: 0.25rem 0.625rem; border: 1px solid var(--input); border-radius: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--foreground); font-family: var(--font-sans), sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; transition: border-color 0.15s ease, box-shadow 0.15s ease; outline: none; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); } .ds-input:disabled { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--input) 50%, transparent); opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Page Eyebrow
components.description: The system's most recognizable typographic signature. Once per page, directly above the display title.
components.html:
HORUS · DIRECTORY

Hacker help, made simple.

components.name: Nav Tab
components.description: The bottom border is always present at 3px; only its color changes on selection, so nothing shifts.

components.name: Avatar
components.description: The only curve in the system. A round shape here means a person.
components.css: .ds-avatar { position: relative; display: flex; width: 2rem; height: 2rem; flex-shrink: 0; border-radius: 9999px; overflow: hidden; user-select: none; } .ds-avatar-fallback { display: flex; width: 100%; height: 100%; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--muted); color: var(--muted-foreground); font-family: var(--font-sans), sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; }

narrative.overview:
Horus is an instrument, not an application. Its job is to let one watcher take in a whole sky at once and know immediately where to point. The interface is accordingly built out of flat, sharp-cornered panels separated by hairlines — readouts on a bench, not cards floating in space. Nothing lifts, nothing glows, nothing rounds itself off to seem friendlier. Density is a feature: the default component text size is 12px and the default control height is 32px, because a helper mid-shift is scanning, not reading.

The one romantic gesture is the type. Page titles and panel titles are set in Lora, a serif — an unusual choice for an operations tool, and the thing that keeps this system from reading as a terminal emulator. That tension is the whole personality: a scholar's hand labelling precise instruments. The serif appears only as a label on a panel; the moment you are inside the panel, everything is Space Grotesk and the numbers take over.

Color is almost entirely spoken for. Emerald, orange and red are not a palette here, they are a vocabulary for ticket state, used identically in a badge, a bar chart, a relative timestamp and a count on the directory. Because those three carry meaning everywhere, the surface underneath them stays quiet — and even the quiet is tinted, every neutral in both themes carrying a faint green hue shift so that white is never quite white and black is never quite black.
keyCharacteristics: Zero corner radius on every surface; circular avatars are the only curve in the system
No box-shadows anywhere — depth is a hairline ring plus a tonal step
Dense by default: 12px component text, 32px control height, 16px panel padding
Serif (Lora) for titles only; sans (Space Grotesk) for everything else
Semantic color triad — emerald / orange / red — reserved for ticket state
Neutrals are hue-shifted toward green (hue 165) in both light and dark
Semantic color arrives as a 10% tinted wash behind its own hue as text, not as a solid fill

rules.name: The Three-State Rule
rules.body: Emerald means resolved, orange means in progress, red means waiting or overdue. These three are spoken for across every surface — badge, chart, count, timestamp, bar. Never use any of them decoratively, and never encode a fourth state in a fourth hue without adding it to this vocabulary first.

rules.name: The Tinted-Fill Rule
rules.body: Semantic color arrives as a 10% wash of itself behind text of the same hue, never as a saturated block. The primary button is the single exception that fills solid — which is precisely what makes it read as the one real action on a screen.

rules.name: The Green Ground Rule
rules.body: Every neutral in this system carries hue 165. Never introduce a pure-gray or blue-gray neutral; it will read as a foreign element against a surface that is quietly green everywhere else.

rules.name: The Serif Label Rule
rules.body: Lora appears only where something is being named: page titles and panel titles. It never appears in body copy, never in data, never in a button, never in a table cell.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Every page opens with HORUS · [SECTION] in uppercase emerald at 0.75rem with 0.1em tracking, directly above the display title. It appears exactly once per page and is the system's most recognizable typographic signature.

rules.name: The 72rem Rule
rules.body: Every page is a centered 72rem column with 2.5rem gutters. Full-bleed content does not exist in this system; a band that spans the viewport still aligns its contents to the column.

rules.name: The Drop-Don't-Squeeze Rule
rules.body: At narrow widths, remove columns rather than shrinking them. A table with four legible columns beats a table with six illegible ones.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Never add a box-shadow to this system. If an element needs to separate from its surroundings, it gets a hairline ring or a tonal step. A shadow anywhere would be the loudest thing on the screen.

rules.name: The Sharp Corner Rule
rules.body: Everything is rounded-none. The radius tokens in the theme are inherited scaffolding and are not to be used. The avatar's circle is the only curve, and it means a person.

rules.name: The Dashed Border Rule
rules.body: A dashed edge means restricted or elevated privilege, always in Restricted Amber, and never anything else.

dos: Do wrap every container in ring-1 ring-foreground/10 rather than a border. It adapts across themes from one declaration.
Do reserve emerald, orange and red for ticket state, in that meaning, on every surface.
Do deliver semantic color as a 10% tint with matching text (bg-destructive/10 text-destructive). Only the primary button fills solid.
Do open every page with the HORUS · [SECTION] eyebrow above a Lora display title.
Do drive panel spacing from --card-spacing instead of hardcoding padding.
Do give loading skeletons the exact dimensions of the content they replace — the existing min-h-72 and h-125 floors exist for this reason.
Do pair every standalone numeral with a 0.75rem uppercase muted caption.
Do mark privileged surfaces with a dashed Restricted Amber border, never with a fill or a color swap.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow. This system has none, and one would dominate everything around it.

Don't add corner radius. Everything is rounded-none; the --radius scale in the theme is inherited scaffolding, not permission. Two existing strays — the instance-card skeleton's rounded-md and the deprecated badge's rounded-bl-md — are drift, not precedent.
Don't use gradients, glassmorphism, blurred floating orbs, or oversized soft corners. (Confirmed anti-reference: the generic AI-era SaaS look.)
Don't introduce a pure-gray neutral. Every neutral here carries hue 165.
Don't set Lora on anything that isn't a page title or a panel title.

Don't use the class text-md. It is undefined in both Tailwind and this project's theme, so it silently does nothing — yet it appears 13 times across the app. Use text-sm or text-base and correct the strays when you touch them.
Don't use a dashed border for anything other than restricted privilege.
Don't compress table columns below 720px — remove them, as the queue table already does.
Don't treat the teal chart ramp as an accent. It exists so decorative series can never be confused with the state triad.
